Scientific Hypothesis: In developing countries, there is a negative relationship between education expenditure (as a percentage of GNI) and per capita GDP. This implies that higher education expenditure may be associated with lower economic output, possibly due to resource allocation inefficiencies or other economic factors. The relationship is statistically significant for Sub-Saharan Africa (correlation coefficient = -0.966) and moderately significant for Lower Middle Income Countries (correlation coefficient = -0.481).
